issue.title: Three tests/test_run_agent_runner_setup_linked_repos.py nodes run the real workspace-occupancy guard against the test process cwd, so they fail on ambient host state
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-qv.1 (epic sase-qv, "Required custom monitor statuses with
deterministic pair colors"), routed here by that epic's land agent. Not caused by
sase-qv: the diff under test was src/sase/monitor_status.py + src/sase/palette_hash.py
plus monitor read paths; nothing in it touches linked-repo setup or workspace occupancy.

OBSERVATION (2026-08-19T13:58:08Z, phase sase-qv.1): three nodes in
tests/test_run_agent_runner_setup_linked_repos.py failed together in an escalated
parallel full suite with WorkspaceOccupiedError naming workspace #0 as "occupied by this
agent", then all three passed on a serial rerun of the same tree:

  - test_prepare_linked_repo_workspaces_uses_default_revision_sentinel
  - test_prepare_linked_repo_workspaces_prepares_retained_sidecar
  - test_prepare_linked_repo_workspaces_failure_names_workspace

ROOT CAUSE (identified by code reading during sase-qv landing, 2026-08-19):
prepare_linked_repo_workspaces_if_needed (src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner_setup.py:157)
declares primary_workspace_dir: str = "" and workspace_num: int = 0, and after
materializing each repo it calls the production occupancy guard
_guard_workspace_not_occupied(checkout_dir=primary_workspace_dir, ...) at
run_agent_runner_setup.py:215. These three tests call the function with only
resolution= and cl_name=, and they patch sase.linked_repos.materialize_linked_repo_workspace
and sase.axe.run_agent_runner_setup.prepare_workspace -- but NOT the guard. So the guard
runs for real with checkout_dir="" and workspace_num=0.

Path("").resolve() is the process cwd, which under pytest is the agent's own sase_<N>
workspace checkout. Verified live on 2026-08-19 from workspace sase_14:

  Path("").resolve() -> /home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_14

so ensure_workspace_not_occupied() reads the live host occupant marker for the very
workspace the test process is running in, and workspace_num=0 is where the "#0" in the
error text comes from. Whether these tests pass therefore depends on ambient host
occupancy state at the moment they run, not on the tree under test. That also explains
the serial-rerun pass: the host's occupant record for that checkout differed by then.
The same probe run today returns no conflict, which is why the nodes are green right now
(12 passed in 3.11s for the whole file).

WHY THIS IS NEW: WorkspaceOccupiedError / ensure_workspace_not_occupied landed recently
(7a2906e13, the sase-q0 "guarantee one agent per workspace" work, ~2026-08-18). Before
that guard existed this call path had no ambient-state read, so these tests were
hermetic. This is a fresh test-isolation regression, not the process-global-state-leak
class that epic sase-j7 owns: nothing leaks between tests here, the test reads real host
state directly.

SCOPE: make the three tests hermetic. Either pass an explicit primary_workspace_dir
(a tmp_path) and workspace_num so the guard checks a scratch directory, or patch
sase.axe.run_agent_runner_setup._guard_workspace_not_occupied for these cases. Prefer
the former, since it also documents the argument the production caller is expected to
supply. While there, audit the other callers of prepare_linked_repo_workspaces_if_needed
in the suite for the same omission, and consider whether checkout_dir="" should be
rejected outright rather than silently resolving to cwd -- a production caller that
forgets primary_workspace_dir would guard the wrong directory the same way.

task_type_fields.evidence: Failed once in an escalated parallel full suite (phase sase-qv.1, 2026-08-19T13:58:08Z), three nodes together, WorkspaceOccupiedError naming "workspace #0 occupied by this agent"; all three passed on a serial rerun of the same tree. Re-run during sase-qv landing on 2026-08-19: 12 passed in 3.11s for the whole file. Not parallel-lane-specific in mechanism -- the guard reads live host occupancy for Path("").resolve() (the test process cwd, i.e. the agent's own sase_<N> checkout), so it can fail serially too whenever that checkout is marked occupied. Fail rate observed: 1 of 2 runs on the same tree.
